note: Rejudged against RFC 9234 Section 5 (lines 383-391): 'On egress from the Internet-facing AS, the OTC Attribute MUST NOT contain a value other than the Internet-facing ASN.' alongside 'Once the OTC Attribute has been set, it MUST be preserved unchanged (this also applies to an AS Confederation).' All four tagged units pass and carry verified discrimination records in rfc/discrimination/rfc9234/RFC9234-5-9.json. Negative unit TestRFC9234PrivateOTCDoesNotLeavePublicEgress isolates privateOTCLeavesPublicAS on a public Customer destination (LocalAS 64497, PeerAS 64498, IsIBGP false) across all four inclusive RFC 6996 Private Use endpoints (64512, 65534, 4200000000, 4294967294), asserting exact rejection and zero OTC rewrite on both direct OTCEgressFilter and forked evaluateRoleFilter paths. Positive units TestPublicOTCBoundaryStillStampsUnmarkedRoutes and TestPrivateOTCBoundaryPreservesOtherSessions close the prior weak finding at the public-to-public eBGP boundary (64497->64498): the former verifies unmarked routes are accepted and stamped with Internet-facing LocalAS 64497 on both direct and forked (FilterModify, otc=64497) paths, while the latter verifies routes carrying Internet-facing local OTC 64497, public upstream OTC 64496, private-ASN sessions, iBGP migration sessions, and withdrawal-only bodies are accepted with OTC preserved unchanged on both paths. TestOTCEgressStampLocalASN additionally distinguishes dest.LocalAS from src.PeerAS and dest.PeerAS during absent-OTC stamping. Together the tagged pair fails on either failure to reject private-domain OTCs at public egress or over-rejection/wrong-ASN stamping of conforming public-boundary routes.
